He talks about how getting under 6.5 hours literally
makes our brain acutely insulin resistant, triggering
constant decision fatigue and craving stimulants.
It traps us in that vicious cycle: stress steals our
sleep, and poor sleep sabotages our resilience.
He suggests approaching your rest like a curious
scientist rather than someone who is broken.
Starting with tiny, gentle levers-like cutting harsh
bathroom overhead lights an hour before bed, or
exploring calming minerals like Magnesium Glycinate
(200-500 mg) to relax tight muscles.
What feels like the loudest thing keeping you wired
when your head finally hits the pillow right now?
